top3.headline: DeepSeek lays out its blueprint for an always-on super-agent
top3.whyItMatters: Its design separates a dispatching router from workers, a pattern worth testing before buying agent platforms.

top3.headline: AI-found bugs delay Postgres 19 as human reviewers fall behind
top3.whyItMatters: Budget reviewer time for AI-found bugs, because drafting fixes is cheap and verifying them is not.

top3.headline: Top AI model scores 12% on a new expert-work benchmark
top3.whyItMatters: SemiAnalysis expects early AI revenue to cluster in sectors with high-return uses, not spread evenly.

items.title: MIT Technology Review: the agentic web has arrived
items.takeaway: Agents browse and act for people without the Semantic Web's tags; the essay weighs effects on the human web.
items.soWhat: Agents now act on websites without special markup, so your site's users increasingly include software.

items.title: Best model scores 12% on SemiAnalysis's new expert-task benchmark
items.takeaway: 206 tasks across 11 domains; Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 12.0%, and finance and legal sit near zero.
items.soWhat: Frontier agents still fail most high-value expert work, so pilot narrow tasks before promising broad savings.

items.title: A protest project uses AI agents to rebuild Auth0 and Salesforce
items.takeaway: Apache-2.0 clean-room replacements written from public API docs and tested against the vendors' own SDKs.
items.soWhat: If agents can rebuild a vendor from its public docs, switching costs for SaaS buyers may fall.

items.title: Calegari: AI has changed mathematics, so act like it
items.takeaway: Guest post calls OpenAI's 700-plus papers a watershed, despite poor writing and attribution.
items.soWhat: When AI output floods a field, leverage shifts to whoever sets the standards for credit and review.

image.alt: Terence Tao's blog: Calegari: AI has changed mathematics, so act like it

items.title: DeepSeek details how it built an always-on agent system
items.takeaway: A router dispatches to isolated workers; in early tests it finished tasks faster than one session.
items.soWhat: Human attention, not agent count, caps how much parallel agent work a team can run.

items.title: Postgres 19 ships late as AI bug reports outpace human review
items.takeaway: Back-patched commits rose from 724 to 1,169 year on year; the release likely lands in November.
items.soWhat: AI finds bugs faster than people can fix them, so review capacity is now the bottleneck.
